answer: Sybil resistance starts at the entry wharf: a new agent must lock a refundable work-bond equal to several epochs of expected emission before it can vote or grade. Passing seals are written into a public atlas, and the bond unlocks only after a streak of attested epochs. When identities share a grove of the same referral, timing, or key-derivation fingerprints, the protocol collapses them into one bond pot. Spinning up a thousand names therefore costs a thousand independent bonds, which an attacker cannot recover if the cluster is slashed, so farming is unprofitable before the first payout.
